content.value_statement: LangChain applications can become hard to structure as agents, tools, memory, and retrieval grow. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical architecture patterns for modular LLM workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains LangChain agents, chains, memory, document processing, and callbacks.
Provides Python examples for conversational agents, RAG, custom tools, and sequential chains.
Compares memory choices for short, long, windowed, entity, and vector-backed conversations.
Shows callback handlers for logging LLM, chain, and agent events.
Covers testing, caching, batch processing, and streaming response patterns.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a complete runnable production application.
Referenced supplemental files are not included in the scanned package.
LangChain import paths may require updates for newer framework versions.
Does not implement authentication, authorization, or secret management.

use_cases.title: Plan a LangChain Agent
use_cases.description: Map agent type, tools, memory, and callback needs before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Design Retrieval Workflows
use_cases.description: Structure document loading, chunking, vector storage, and source-aware retrieval flows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Review testing, observability, rate limits, error handling, and performance practices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a first LangChain agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a simple LangChain agent for my task. Include the agent type, required tools, memory choice, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a LangChain RAG workflow for these documents and questions. Recommend loaders, splitters, vector storage, retrieval settings, and source handling.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Memory Strategies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate architecture choice for conversational systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare LangChain memory options for my chat application. Explain tradeoffs for cost, context length, accuracy, and implementation complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my LangChain architecture for production. Check agents, tools, prompts, memory, callbacks, testing, rate limits, and observability.

output_examples.input: Design a support assistant that can search policies and answer follow-up questions.
output_examples.output: A recommended architecture with a conversational agent, policy retriever, windowed memory, callback logging, and tests for tool selection.

output_examples.input: Choose memory for a customer onboarding chat that may last many turns.
output_examples.output: A comparison of buffer, summary, window, entity, and vector memory with a recommended hybrid approach.

output_examples.input: Review my LangChain pipeline before launch.
output_examples.output: A production checklist covering validation, error handling, observability, token costs, streaming behavior, and fallback strategy.

best_practices: Define tool descriptions clearly so agents select the right action.
Limit memory growth with summaries, windows, or retrieval-backed history.
Add callbacks and tests before deploying agent workflows.
anti_patterns: Giving agents broad tool access without validation or approval steps.
Storing full conversation history without token or privacy limits.
Shipping retrieval workflows without source checks or evaluation tests.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design LangChain applications with agents, chains, memory, retrieval, callbacks, testing, and performance patterns.

faq.question: Does it write complete application code?
faq.answer: It provides architecture guidance and example patterns. You still need to adapt the implementation to your application.

faq.question: Can I use it for RAG applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a RAG pattern with loaders, splitters, embeddings, vector storage, retrievers, and source document handling.

faq.question: Does it cover memory management?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains buffer, summary, window, entity, and vector retriever memory choices.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install automatically?
faq.answer: The reviewed file is documentation only. It does not include executable install scripts or shell commands.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
